source: NDMA — National Disaster Management Authority preparedness guidance (public safety steps; bundled for fully offline access)

cyclone.title: Cyclone
before: Assemble an emergency kit: torch, battery radio, spare batteries, first-aid, 3 days of drinking water and dry food.
Charge mobile phones and power banks fully; keep a power bank in your kit.
Secure loose objects on balconies and rooftops; trim dead branches near the house.
Locate your nearest cyclone shelter and the evacuation route to it.
Keep documents (ID, land records, insurance) in a waterproof bag.
Fishermen: do not venture into the sea while a cyclone warning is active.
during: Stay indoors, away from doors and windows; shelter in the strongest room on the ground floor.
If coastal storm-surge evacuation is advised, move to the designated shelter immediately — do not wait.
Disconnect electrical appliances; do not touch wet switches.
Do NOT go outside during the sudden lull — that is the eye of the storm; winds return violently from the opposite direction.
Keep the radio on for official updates; ignore rumors.
after: Stay inside until the official all-clear is issued.
Avoid floodwater, fallen power lines and damaged buildings.
Boil all drinking water; discard food touched by floodwater.
Report casualties and damage on 1078 (NDMA helpline) or 112.
Check on elderly, disabled and pregnant neighbours.

flood.title: Flood
before: Move medicines, documents and valuables to upper floors.
Know how to switch off electricity and gas at the mains — do it the moment water enters the house.
Stock drinking water, dry food and a torch with spare batteries.
Keep a rope, inflatable ring and plastic sheets ready.
Identify the highest reachable ground and the route to it.
during: Move to higher ground immediately; do not wait for water to reach the door.
NEVER walk or drive through flowing water — 15 cm can sweep you off your feet, 60 cm can float a car.
Stay away from electric poles, transformers and submerged wiring.
If swept away, float on your back with feet pointing downstream.
Abandon belongings — life first.
after: Do not return home until authorities declare it safe.
Boil or disinfect every drop of drinking water; wash all utensils.
Discard all food touched by floodwater.
Beware of snakes and insects sheltering indoors.
Report waterlogging and disease symptoms to the local authority.

heatwave.title: Heat Wave
before: Hydrate through the day — water, ORS, buttermilk, lemon water — even if not thirsty.
Avoid alcohol, tea and coffee during peak hours; they dehydrate.
Wear light-coloured, loose cotton clothes; use a wide-brim hat or umbrella outdoors.
Schedule outdoor work and travel before 11:00 or after 16:00.
Check on infants, the elderly and the chronically ill twice a day.
during: Stay indoors between 12:00 and 16:00; keep curtains closed on sun-facing sides.
Cool the body: wet cloth on neck and wrists, cool baths, fans with cross-ventilation.
Sweating heavily? Drink ORS — plain water alone can dilute body salts.
Heat stroke signs: body temperature above 40°C, confusion, dry skin with NO sweating — cool aggressively (ice packs to armpits/groin) and call 108 immediately.
Never leave children or pets inside a parked vehicle.
after: Rest in a cool place for at least 24 hours after severe heat exposure.
Continue steady hydration for the next two days.
Watch children and the elderly for delayed dehydration symptoms.
Re-check your heat plan before the next peak-heat day.

lightning.title: Lightning
before: Track IMD thunderstorm alerts; plan field work and outdoor events around them.
Know the 30-30 rule: if thunder follows lightning within 30 seconds, go indoors — stay 30 minutes after the last thunder.
Identify safe shelters along your usual routes: buildings, hard-topped vehicles.
Teach children: 'When thunder roars, go indoors.'
during: Get inside a substantial building or a hard-topped metal vehicle; close the windows.
Once inside: stay away from windows, plumbing taps and wired electronics; unplug appliances.
Caught in the open? Crouch low on the balls of your feet, feet together, head down — do NOT lie flat.
Avoid tall isolated trees, poles, fences, metal rails and all water bodies.
Cattle and people are killed under trees — never shelter there.
after: Lightning-strike victims carry NO electric charge — touch and help them immediately.
If the victim is unconscious and not breathing, start CPR and call 108.
Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before resuming outdoor activity.
Check cattle and livestock in open fields.
